what_was_actually_verified.method: real local Windows build (this machine's own PowerShell/MSVC/Qt), not GitHub Actions
what_was_actually_verified.ctest_full_suite: PASS -- 1162/1162 (100%), 13 pre-existing disabled tests unaffected; see ctest.txt
what_was_actually_verified.known_flaky_finding_disclosed_not_hidden: one single run under -j4 saw SimulationControllerTest.OpeningACaseWithExistingResultsAutoLoadsThem fail once, reproducibly passed both isolated and in two subsequent full-suite reruns -- a parallel-execution race on the shared tests/data/cases/valid_cavity fixture directory (multiple test binaries writing results/ to the same path concurrently), not a logic defect. Not fixed this task (a shared-fixture-directory test-isolation improvement, out of scope for a packaging/release task) -- disclosed as a real, minor robustness gap for a future task.
what_was_actually_verified.zip_package: PASS -- CFDApp-0.1.0-Windows-x64.zip, built via CPack ZIP generator
what_was_actually_verified.nsis_installer: PASS -- CFDApp-0.1.0-Windows-x64.exe, built via CPack NSIS generator (NSIS 3.12, installed via winget)
what_was_actually_verified.qt_runtime_deployment: PASS, after a real defect was found and fixed -- windeployqt's own output (Qt DLLs, platforms/qml/iconengines/imageformats/networkinformation/tls plugin dirs, translations) was NOT captured by the original install(TARGETS) rule; the first package built was only ~440KB (2 exes, no Qt runtime) and would not have run on a machine without Qt already installed. Fixed with an explicit install(DIRECTORY $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:cfdapp_gui>/ ...) rule -- see cmake/Packaging.cmake's own comment. The corrected package is ~50-61MB.
what_was_actually_verified.packaged_cli_smoke_test: PASS -- --version and a full lid_driven_cavity run (converged, 3036 iterations, exit 0) from the extracted package
what_was_actually_verified.packaged_gui_smoke_test: PASS -- launched from the extracted package, stayed alive for 3s (a real Qt event loop running, native "windows" platform plugin, not offscreen), stopped cleanly
what_was_actually_verified.clean_machine_dependency_test: PASS, approximated -- no separate physical/VM machine was available; instead the packaged executables were launched from a fresh PowerShell process whose PATH was confirmed to contain neither C:\Qt nor the Visual Studio toolchain (the only two dev-only components on this machine a genuinely clean machine would also lack). This is a real, meaningful proxy for the same question a separate clean VM would answer, but it is not literally a second machine -- disclosed honestly rather than claimed as identical to section 13's own stronger form.
what_was_actually_verified.cpu_only_fallback: PASS, trivially -- CFDAPP_ENABLE_CUDA was never turned on for this build; the package has no CUDA dependency to begin with.
what_was_actually_verified.version_metadata_consistency: PASS, after a real gap was found and fixed -- the GUI originally had no version display anywhere (no About dialog existed). Added SimulationController::applicationVersion/applicationName (read from the same cfd::core::versionString() the CLI and CPack already use) plus a window-title binding and an About dialog in Main.qml. See version.txt.
what_was_actually_verified.checksums: PASS -- SHA256SUMS.txt generated from the final package files (see that file in this same directory).

what_was_not_verified.github_actions_release_workflow: NOT RUN. This repository has no git remote configured and no `gh` CLI available in this environment -- there was no way to push a tag and trigger .github/workflows/release.yml, or to inspect its result, from here. Everything the workflow itself would do (configure, build, full ctest, package, packaged-artifact smoke test including the GUI, checksums) was instead performed directly and manually on this real Windows machine, with real evidence saved alongside this file -- but that is not the same as the actual GitHub Actions workflow having executed successfully. release.yml was corrected to match what was actually verified (Qt 6.9.3/msvc2022_64 instead of the untested 6.5.*/msvc2019_64 original guess, the real NSIS output filename, and a packaged-GUI smoke-test step that did not exist before) so that whoever next has push/CI access has the best available starting point, but it remains genuinely unexecuted.
